criteria.justification: The response explicitly says, “Speed was never the main complaint” and “I optimized for the wrong pain,” treating the false-positive data as an independent reason to reconsider. It further notes that consolidation “just made it urgent,” rather than presenting consolidation as the sole cause.

It clearly separates the expiring speed narrative from potentially reusable technical value: “Some of that investment may transfer. The narrative doesn't.” It also considers retaining the architecture as a standalone product or folding its precision capability into the consolidated pipeline.

The response directly identifies the prior investment as sunk and reframes the decision around future value: “The right question isn't ‘how do we justify what we built?’” It likewise accepts that the best outcome may involve losing ownership of a standalone product.

It engages the peer’s precision thesis on the merits and candidly acknowledges, “The peer was right, and I should say so.” The response also proposes involving that peer because they have already thought deeply about the problem.

The response commits to pausing the speed-based launch, running a concrete 4–6 week validation sprint, and reframing around precision if supported by customer interviews and backtesting. It provides explicit decision paths—standalone, integrated precision layer, or wind-down—based on defined evidence and metrics.
